purpose: Assess whether protest/sensitive-event timing correlates with network restrictions and whether observed mechanisms can be causally connected to Russian-origin SORM/DPI technology. Preserve strict separation between confirmed network behavior, vendor lineage, and remote-control attribution.

network_structure.operator: Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Cuba S.A. (ETECSA)
network_structure.structure: state-owned telecommunications monopoly / overwhelmingly dominant public connectivity provider
network_structure.2026_apnic_estimate: AS27725 approximately 97.9% of estimated Cuban Internet users in July 2026
network_structure.implication: A restriction implemented at or through ETECSA can have near-national effect without cross-ISP coordination. This is a centralized-control positive control, not evidence of Russian command.

technical_baseline.event: OONI censorship study in Cuban public-access ParkNets
technical_baseline.finding: 41 websites confirmed blocked. DPI middlebox reset connections and served blank block pages; latency localized blocking infrastructure most likely to Havana. Skype blocking used injected TCP RST packets. Other services such as WhatsApp and Facebook Messenger remained accessible in that measurement period.

technical_baseline.event: Movimiento San Isidro protest / artistic-freedom mobilization
technical_baseline.finding: NetBlocks measured social-media disruptions on ETECSA/AS27725; Freedom House reports widespread mobile and home connectivity interruptions and many localized mobile-service disruptions after the protest.

ETECSA cut island-wide Internet service for about 30 minutes on the first major protest day, followed by intermittent outages and prolonged restoration. OONI detected WhatsApp/Telegram/Signal blocking; reported mechanism included TCP RST injection during TLS handshake. NetBlocks localized restrictions to ETECSA/AS27725 and Cubacel, including WhatsApp, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram servers, YouTube and Google Video. IODA, Cloudflare/Fastly traffic and Google traffic data independently showed disruption.

technical_baseline.event: protests following Hurricane Ian and prolonged power failures
technical_baseline.finding: Freedom House and US State reporting describe overnight Internet cuts lasting about seven hours on two successive nights, while authorities also used regional/individual restrictions during protests.

Livestreams of protests circulated before mobile connectivity was reportedly disrupted nationwide. US State and Freedom House describe ETECSA as regularly cutting or restricting connections during protests.

technical_baseline.event: protests in Santiago de Cuba and other eastern localities over electricity and food shortages
technical_baseline.finding: Internet Society Pulse records a regional shutdown in at least two regions from 15:20 to 20:30 UTC, about five hours, with measured traffic dip during the protest window.

technical_baseline.event: Havana-area protests over blackouts and water shortages
technical_baseline.finding: Independent Cuban media reported mobile/data outages beginning around protest gatherings. IODA-derived reporting detected significant connectivity drops across multiple provinces on June 20, but the incident lacks ASN-specific mechanism attribution and power-grid instability is a major confound.

russian_lineage.recorded_future_2025: Insikt Group assessed Cuba very likely procured SORM hardware and software from Russian companies, most notably Protei.
russian_lineage.customer_bridge: Protei company materials identify ETECSA as a customer; Recorded Future Appendix B lists ETECSA Cuba as a Protei customer.
russian_lineage.2024_bridge: Protei signed an agreement with Cuban state-owned Movitel in March 2024 to facilitate construction of private network systems following Informática 2024 in Havana.
protections_against_overclaim: Protei sells products unrelated to SORM, so ETECSA customer status does not prove which product was installed.
Recorded Future's assessment of SORM procurement is high-value vendor-lineage evidence, not proof that the protest-day blocking middlebox was Protei.
No verified public evidence currently links a specific 2017/2020/2021/2024 RST or shutdown event to a Protei device serial, management server, firmware image, or Russian control point.
No verified public evidence establishes Moscow remote command of Cuban filtering.
The user's remembered 'one box' shipment may correspond to prior trade/vendor evidence, but the literal count of one shipped device was not verified in this pass.

non_russian_lineage_and_controls.china: Cuban telecommunications infrastructure has substantial Chinese vendor presence, including Huawei and ZTE; this is a major alternative technology lineage and prevents simplistic attribution to Russia.
non_russian_lineage_and_controls.avila_link: Cuba has reportedly used Ávila Link monitoring software at ETECSA/public access points; provenance and relation to specific blocking events require separate validation.
non_russian_lineage_and_controls.power_grid: Cuba's chronic grid failures and nationwide electricity collapses can independently reduce Internet traffic and must be treated as a primary negative control, especially in 2022, 2024 and 2026 protest windows.
non_russian_lineage_and_controls.monopoly_effect: Because ETECSA dominates national access, nationwide effects can result from domestic centralized policy without any foreign control-plane involvement.

cisa_trigger_evaluation.us_service_nexus: PASS_HISTORICAL: US-origin/global platforms such as WhatsApp/Facebook/Instagram/YouTube/Google were selectively disrupted during protest windows
cisa_trigger_evaluation.negative_controls: PARTIAL_PASS: independent measurement and service selectivity exist, but some event windows have power-grid confounds
cisa_trigger_evaluation.independent_replication: PASS_HISTORICAL: OONI, NetBlocks, IODA, traffic telemetry, Freedom House/State documentation
cisa_trigger_evaluation.vendor_control_plane_bridge: PARTIAL_PASS: Russian SORM/Protei procurement/customer relationship is strongly supported, but causal connection to blocking devices is not established

next_measurements: Obtain raw OONI measurements for July 2021 and March 2024 and cluster by test_name, failure type, ASN and protocol phase.
Compare TCP RST TTL/IPID/timing characteristics from 2017 and July 2021 to test whether the same middlebox family persisted.
For June 19-20 2026, align IODA provincial drops with protest timestamps and electricity-restoration timestamps to separate policy restriction from power loss.
Inspect AS27725 BGP/traffic telemetry during protest windows and matched non-protest blackout controls.
Search archived Protei/ETECSA/Movitel technical materials for exact product names, deployments, lawful-intercept interfaces, maintenance/control architecture, and dates.
Do not elevate to Russian-control attribution without device/operator/control-channel evidence.
final_rule: Cuba is a strong positive control for protest-conditioned centralized network restriction and a high-value Russian SORM vendor-lineage case. It is not public proof that Russian SORM performed the observed blocking and is not evidence of Russian remote control.
